evidence.reason: The finding targets an explicitly accepted, documented limitation rather than an implementation defect. The quoted region of `src/driver/README.md` (lines 498–503) states that on POSIX the CLI child is spawned detached and the whole group is signalled, while "Windows has no Job Object in v1 (descendants can survive there — recorded limitation in `src/shared/proc.ts`; the supported descendant-cleanup guarantee is POSIX-only until independently proven on Windows)." The finding itself concedes the README correctly describes the guarantee as POSIX-only and that no process-group signalling exists on win32. Its requested remedy — "Add Windows descendant cleanup that matches the POSIX process-group behavior" — is a proposal to add or enlarge a requirement (Windows Job Object support), not a repair of existing intended behavior. The current contract does not mandate Windows descendant cleanup; the recorded v1 scope is POSIX-only. An opportunity to harden an accepted limitation does not itself establish a defect.
